calibrationRunBeforeFalsifierLocked.purpose: Establish the baseline null-rate of candidate recovery fields inside the KNOWN-PURE lineage (hays-export2.zip, never touched by P-78) before trusting any field as a discriminator. This is baseline calibration, not a peek at the answer under test -- the untouched lineage's own null-rate is the control, independent of what the StratMap-tagged rows will show.
calibrationRunBeforeFalsifierLocked.query: SELECT source_file, count(*) n, count(assessed_value) n_assessed_not_null, count(*) FILTER (WHERE exemption_codes IS NOT NULL AND array_length(exemption_codes,1)>0) n_exempt_not_null, count(living_area_sqft) n_living_area_not_null FROM cad_property WHERE county_fips='48209' AND tax_year=2025 GROUP BY source_file -- live, f06-staging-neondb (database neondb), 2026-09-09
calibrationRunBeforeFalsifierLocked.fieldSelected: assessed_value. Reason: its baseline null-rate in the known-pure CAD lineage is exactly 0% -- every genuine Hays CAD account carries an assessed value, so IS NOT NULL has no false negatives against the reference population. exemption_codes (60.6% baseline) and living_area_sqft (71.2% baseline) are legitimately sparse even in pure CAD rows (vacant land, no-exemption accounts), so a NULL there does not imply non-CAD -- they are weaker, not usable as the primary discriminator.
calibrationRunBeforeFalsifierLocked.independentCrossCheck: 75551 (direct count of assessed_value IS NOT NULL among stratmap-tagged 2025 rows) EXACTLY equals 131246-55695=75551, where 131246 is the pre-P78 CAD-only population figure the P-78 announce doc itself reports as the 'before' count (_inbox/2026-08-25_p78_announce_hays_48209.md) and 55695 is the live count of rows still tagged hays-export2.zip today. Two independently derived numbers -- one from a historical apply-log arithmetic, one from a live field-null count -- agree exactly. Likewise 116421-75551=40870 exactly matches the announce doc's own '40870 new keys @ 2025' line.

preRegisteredFalsifier.claimUnderTest: assessed_value IS NOT NULL, applied to rows currently tagged source_file='stratmap25-landparcels_48209_lp.zip' at tax_year=2025, recovers which of those rows were genuine pre-existing CAD accounts (source_file overwritten by P-78) versus genuinely new StratMap-only geometry rows (never a CAD account).
preRegisteredFalsifier.wouldShowSeparable: The count of stratmap-tagged rows with assessed_value IS NOT NULL lands at or very near 75551 (already observed above, pre-registered as the target band: within a few hundred rows, allowing for ordinary roll churn) AND the known-pure lineage's own assessed_value null-rate stays at or near 0%.
preRegisteredFalsifier.wouldShowNOTSeparable: (a) the stratmap-tagged assessed_value-not-null count is far off 75551 (would mean the field does not cleanly track pre-P78 CAD membership), OR (b) the pure hays-export2.zip lineage itself shows a material assessed_value null-rate (would mean NULL does not reliably imply 'never CAD' -- some genuine CAD accounts are legitimately null too, so the recovered split would have unquantified false negatives).
preRegisteredFalsifier.conclusionIfItFires: Report that source_file cannot be trusted alone (already established) AND that assessed_value also fails as a clean recovery field; state whatever partial/probabilistic signal remains, do not force a split the data cannot support, and say plainly that the two lineages are not cleanly separable post-overwrite for the affected rows.

controlCountyPlan.why: Per the original finding's full 40-county sweep, Bastrop is one of the 34 single-vintage counties: tax_year=2025 only, from one source, no tax_year=2026 row exists to compare against.
controlCountyPlan.planForTheAntijoinPart: A literal present@2025/absent@2026 antijoin against Bastrop is structurally vacuous (there is no 2026 row for ANY Bastrop prop_id, so 100% of the 2025 population trivially qualifies as 'absent') -- that outcome is not a bug, it is the correct and expected result of running the instrument against a county with no second vintage, and will be reported as such rather than mistaken for a finding.
controlCountyPlan.planForTheMeaningfulControl: The part of the instrument actually under test here is the source_file GROUP BY -- confirm that a county known (from the prior lane's live sweep) to hold a single lineage returns EXACTLY one distinct source_file covering 100% of its rows, with no spurious fragmentation (e.g. whitespace/case variants of one true source read as multiple). This is the real single-lineage validation; a result of more than one group, or less than 100% coverage by the top group, would mean the counting logic itself is unsound and no Hays result from it should be trusted.
